title: 回测与效果评估
summary: 比较资源预测与实际用量，理解准确度、误差和算法排名。
text: 时间滚动回测 回测沿时间顺序移动预测起点，每次仅使用起点之前的历史。训练与评估窗口应与实际使用场景一致；参与指标也必须按相同起点截取。 理解资源预测表现 准确度针对 CPU、内存、GPU 等资源。副本数量由资源需求和约束推出，阅读时应与实际副本及 Ready 状态区分。 指标 含义与用途 WAPE 绝对误差总和与实际值绝对总和的比例，比较同一窗口的预测偏差。 峰值低估 关注预测低于实际高水位的风险，避免平均误差掩盖峰值问题。 资源准确度与综合评分 结合资源表现、完整度及保护因素阅读；评分高不等于可以跳过执行边界。 实测评估 目标时间到达后，用采集到的实际用量关联预测。 评分、排名与共识 算法评分与排名页可以查看当前表现和历史变化。排名帮助比较候选；前瞻决策综合可用预测及可信度形成共识，不只是跟随排名第一的算法。 结合训练与运行明细核对历史窗口、参数版本、耗时和原因。新配置应重新检查效果，避免直接沿用旧配置的结论。 等待实际值与持续评估 尚未到达目标时间的预测没有对应实际值，不能解释为零误差。数据质量、负载规律和预测视野变化后，需要继续观察资源表现和执行结果。 按模块阅读预测效果报告 在预测结果的效果报告中选择模块和时间范围，汇总资源预测误差、峰值低估、扩容及时性、超配与不足、反复扩缩、降级原因和算法采用情况。样本不足与无法测算分别说明，不把没有数据当成零误差。 实际 Pod·小时与容量 SLO 执行与容量一节对照实测 Ready 副本与负载折算的需要副本，给出实际、需要、多占和不足的 Pod·小时，以及容量不足分钟数。数据缺口不计入已对照时间。 容量 SLO 是“没有容量不足的时间 ÷ 已对照时间”，默认目标 99%，可通过 forecast.slo_capacity_target_percent 配置。这不是延迟或错误率 SLO；多占的 Pod·小时也不等于已经节省的费用。至少 12 个对照时刻且覆盖统计范围的一半，才给出数值。 变更影响预览 在效果报告中打开变更预览，用相同历史比较保存的配置和拟改配置，查看不足或超配窗口、风险误差、副本·小时、变化次数和差异最大的时刻。可比较算法及参数、安全余量、单 Pod 容量、副本边界与短期修正。 预览只读，不保存推荐、不修改模块，也不执行伸缩。当前比较的是预测折算的副本数，未完整重放冷却、步长、前瞻与保护规则；模型服务使用预训练模型，不使用后台微调副本。结合这些范围解释结果。

title: 资源推荐与前瞻决策
summary: 理解多算法共识、提前量和各项约束如何形成最终建议。
text: 阅读推荐快照 一份推荐保存某次计算的资源建议、目标副本、决定因素、采用来源、版本与有效期。它回答“建议怎么配”和“为什么”，执行记录回答“最终是否应用”。 为容量就绪预留时间 需求出现时才发起扩容，新增 Pod 可能来不及就绪。前瞻决策把采集、预测、控制循环、Pod Ready 及需要时的节点准备时间纳入提前量，再检查相应未来窗口。 扩容与缩容关注的窗口不同。缩容需要更谨慎地结合未来需求、当前负载与就绪状态，避免将短暂回落解释为可以立即减少容量。 多算法共识 所有可用候选都可参与提前量窗口的计算，可信度结合评分与近期跟踪误差。决策按配置的加权分位数汇总候选，再结合实测负载与安全约束结算。 共识说明应与最终副本、约束、当前用量一起阅读。没有可用预测时，按模块规则进入固定周期、兜底或保持原值。 资源与副本约束 CPU、内存、吞吐和 JVM 压力可能成为决定性约束。 副本受最小值、最大值、硬上限、步长与冷却限制。 OOM 地板和内存峰值提供保护，不能由平滑的点预测替代。 单 Pod 容量来自配置或历史估计，需要结合业务压测确认。 建议、写入与就绪是不同阶段 目标副本已经提交，不代表 Pod 已经 Ready。结合实际副本、就绪状态与后续资源表现判断效果。 预测要覆盖容量准备时间 需要规划副本伸缩时，实际预测范围会结合模块预测周期、运行间隔和提前量扩展，默认按两倍提前量覆盖，最长不超过 24 小时；推荐明细说明扩展原因。已有足够扩容结果时，提前量优先参考本模块实测的容量就绪时间，并吸收近期扩容偏晚的余量。 近期跟踪明显落后的候选，在存在健康候选时不参与共识。若实时负载已超过预测与当前容量，可由可配置的紧急扩容规则兜底；紧急路径只允许扩容，仍受副本上限约束。

title: 资源准入与弹性伸缩
summary: 分别开放新 Pod 资源配置与副本调整，追踪实际执行结果。
text: 让 Operator 调整副本 配置目标工作负载、副本上下界、扩缩容步长和冷却时间。模块和全局开关均授权 Auto 后，Operator 才依据有效建议执行。 直接在平台模块上管理：Operator 读取模块并写副本，不在集群里创建任何资源。同一个目标只能有一个副本所有者。 同一目标只有一个控制者 不能让 Operator 与 HPA、KEDA 或重复 scaler 同时写同一工作负载的副本。切换前先停止原控制器并释放控制权，再检查新控制器的观察结果。 为新 Pod 应用资源建议 准入路径只读取最新有效推荐，按配置调整新 Pod 的 CPU / 内存 requests，以及允许的 limits。推荐不可用时保留原资源，避免阻塞发布。 推荐更新不会立即改变运行中的 Pod。通过新建或滚动更新应用配置，调低内存 limits 前需单独评估和授权。 检查实际效果 在执行、准入及相关明细中查看建议、应用结果、暂停或失败原因。继续检查实际与 Ready 副本、负载和资源用量，区分配置提交成功与容量就绪。 扩容是否赶上了负载 在扩容记录中打开“扩容及时性”，查看及时率、迟到时长 P90、实时兜底占比、峰值低估 P90、预测范围与提前量之比，以及决策等待时间。每项显示样本量与判定；样本不足时为待积累，配置满足要求不等于扩容效果已经达标。 向上决策会结合后续实际负载与 Ready 副本，区分及时、偏晚和负载未到来。已评估的就绪与迟到时长反馈到后续提前量；当前这类结果评估针对扩容，不代表缩容效果。 失联期间的执行记录补报 Operator 先把上报放入发件箱，平台恢复后按发生顺序补报。设置 --report-spool-file 可写入挂载文件，部署清单提供 emptyDir：同一个 Pod 内容器重启可保留，Pod 被替换后不保证保留。 队列最多 10,000 条，超出丢最早记录并计数；平台明确拒绝的记录会被移除，避免阻塞后续记录。文件不是无限保留的审计存储。 执行记录可选列包括 record_id 、动作时间、上报时间、决策来源、失联状态与 Operator 标识。平台按记录 ID 去重，迟到上报仍按实际发生时间归档。 Request、Limit 比例与 OOM 地板 模块配置 Limit 比例时，按最终 Request 计算：例如内存 Request 为 10 GiB，比例 1.2，Limit 为 12 GiB。OOM 系数抬高 Request 的保护地板，不再与 Limit 比例重复叠加。 准入询问携带 request_uid 和 operation 后才能关联调用来源并去重；没有请求 UID 的查询仍返回建议，但不生成准入记录。

title: 安全边界与故障回退
summary: 配置固定周期、兜底、旁路和保护策略，控制自动行为。
text: 模式与授权 Observe 和 Recommend 帮助积累判断依据。资源准入与自动伸缩由对应全局开关和模块模式共同控制，默认关闭写入。放开某项能力前，先确认目标、权限与资源边界。 固定周期规则 为明确的保障时段设置资源或副本固定值，注明起止、时区、优先级和覆盖字段。未覆盖字段仍按其余规则处理；规则结束后再回到正常计算。 调度周期使用显式 IANA 时区，存储保持 UTC。平台默认时区为 UTC+8，页面固定以 UTC+8 展示，不能将显示时间再次写回存储。 降级与恢复 字段按“旁路 → 固定周期 → 合格算法 → 模块兜底 → 保持原值”判断。所有建议仍需合法、有效且符合上下界；OOM 地板对旁路之外的来源生效。 历史不足、输入陈旧、算法失败或没有合格预测时，记录具体原因。恢复需要连续健康周期，避免在异常边缘频繁切换。 需要人工接管时 为目标模块启用 Bypass，说明原因。 关闭相应全局开关，恢复 Recommend 或 Observe。 检查快照、执行记录和实际资源。 修复输入或策略，重新比较效果后逐步恢复授权。 停止后续动作，不会撤销既有变化 旁路和开关不会自动恢复先前副本或资源配置。结合当前服务状态和操作记录处理恢复。 单独配置 OOM 内存保护 模块将 OOM 保护与预测指标分开管理：配置回看天数、内存提升系数和堆压力，并单独接入 OOM 次数、OOM 前工作集、内存 limits 与 JVM 堆指标。未接入对应指标的规则不会生效，推荐说明会标明缺失。 OOM 评分加权默认关闭。启用后，仅在评估窗口内存配置不足时扣减内存得分，不扣 CPU 得分；内存地板与模型评分分别承担保护和比较职责。 平台失联时的保持、降级与恢复 Operator 为每个模块分别记录状态，连接故障不会立即把副本切到兜底值。时间限制在系统参数中维护，由平台下发；以下为默认行为。 状态 副本行为 正常 使用平台决策，受模块边界、冷却与步长约束。 缓存接管 最后一次成功响应未满 10 分钟时使用缓存，只上调、不下调，不继承紧急标记。 保持 没有有效缓存时，先保持当前副本 5 分钟，不立即套兜底。 降级 保持期结束后，按兜底值单步上调，不低于当前副本，两次调整间遵守降级冷却。 恢复中 平台重新响应后，上调可跟随；下调同时要求连续 2 次成功响应及至少 5 分钟稳定期。 决策缓存、模块配置缓存、保持期、降级冷却、恢复响应次数和稳定期分别通过 operator.decision_cache_ttl_seconds 、 module_cache_ttl_seconds 、 degrade_hold_seconds 、 degrade_cooldown_seconds 、 recover_answers 、 recover_stable_seconds 配置，均使用 operator. 前缀。模块配置也失效时保持副本。平台明确回答“无决策”优先于旧缓存，不会被旧建议替代。 决策缓存仅在内存中，重启后不保留；离线执行记录可单独落盘，见 离线补报 。

title: AI 助手与 Skill
summary: 查询平台状态、使用斜杠技能，导出报告并解读资源变化。
text: 打开 AI 助手 管理员在系统参数中启用 assistant.enabled ，并为用户授予 assistant:chat 按钮权限后，右上角显示助手入口。对话在浮动窗口中进行；关闭总开关后入口和窗口都会隐藏。模型连接与技能在“AI 配置”菜单管理。 可以直接提问：“哪些模块需要关注？”“订单服务最近的扩容是否及时？”“平台失联期间 Operator 做了什么？”助手按需读取平台已存的模块、效果报告、伸缩与准入记录，并将结果组织成回答。 用斜杠命令完成常见查询 输入 / 查看可用技能，使用方向键选择，Enter 执行、Tab 补全、Esc 关闭列表。管理员禁用的技能不会出现在可用列表中。 命令 用途 需要 LLM /help 列出可用技能与参数说明。 否 /report 生成近 24 小时使用报告，提供文档与 JSON 下载。 否 /export 导出近 24 小时服务运行状态。 否 /tasks 查看自己的 AI 定时任务、下次运行与最近结果。 否 /attention 分析需要关注的模块及原因。 是 /outage 检查平台失联、离线补报和降级情况。 是 /actions [模块] 解读伸缩动作，可指定模块。 是 /effect <模块> 解读指定模块的预测效果。 是，模块必填 /admission 解读准入决策记录。 是 报告与导出直接根据平台记录生成，没有配置 LLM 时也可使用；总开关和访问权限仍需满足。 管理和编写 Skill 在“AI 配置 → Skill 管理”维护技能。内置技能可启用或禁用，提示词只读；需要模型的技能可指定 LLM，未指定时使用默认模型。内置技能不能删除。 自定义技能配置命令、标题、描述、参数模式（不带参数、必填或可选）、模型和提示词。用 {{args}} 引用命令后的输入。例如创建 /review ，要求模块参数，并使用以下提示词： Text 复制 请分析模块 {{args}} 最近 24 小时的预测效果与伸缩记录，区分已知事实、可能原因和缺少的数据。 保存并启用后，聊天命令列表即可使用该技能。指定的模型须可用；技能没有自己的模型时跟随默认连接。 回答范围与操作能力 助手查询已有记录，不修改算法参数、工作负载资源或副本。数值预测仍由预测算法与时序模型计算，执行仍经过平台规则和 Operator。自然语言解释应与对应记录一起阅读。 对话可创建、查看和删除用户自己的 AI 定时任务 ；这类任务只查询平台并发送回答，不执行资源变更。聊天创建任务只发送到当前用户自己的邮箱。 聊天、技能和导出使用 assistant:chat 权限；LLM 管理、Skill 管理与任务管理分别授权。助手当前可读取平台范围的数据，不能将聊天权限理解为仅能读取个人名下模块。 无法提问时检查什么 没有入口：检查总开关与聊天权限。 报告可用但提问失败：检查默认 LLM 是否启用、地址与模型名称、工具调用兼容性及密钥。 技能未显示：检查是否禁用；需要参数的命令先补齐参数。 回答缺少信息：核对平台本身是否已有对应时间范围的采集、推荐与执行记录。

title: LLM 连接配置
summary: 设置默认与指定模型、工具调用、高级参数和凭据。
text: 添加语言模型连接 在“AI 配置 → LLM 管理”新增连接，填写名称、提供商类型、接口基础地址、模型标识与密钥，再使用“测试连接”检查当前表单内容。地址通常包含服务要求的 API 前缀，例如 /v1 ，不要填入完整的聊天接口路径。 当前提供商类型为 OpenAI 兼容协议。支持该协议的网关或自托管服务可配置接入；Anthropic、Gemini 原生协议不在当前提供商类型中。所选模型需要支持工具调用，才能按需查询平台数据。 启用、默认与指定模型 多个连接可以同时启用。普通提问、未指定模型的 Skill 和定时任务使用默认连接；没有显式默认时，使用最早启用的连接。默认连接必须启用。Skill 与定时任务也可单独指定模型。 LLM 管理只管理语言模型。预测管理中的“模型管理”配置 Chronos 等时序模型，负责生成数值预测，两类连接分别维护。 高级设置 设置 作用 请求超时 默认 90 秒，范围 5～600 秒，限制单次模型请求。 工具读取轮数 默认 6，范围 1～12，限制一次提问中模型继续调用工具的轮数。 Temperature 可选，控制回答采样；是否生效取决于服务对该字段的支持。 最大 Tokens 限制单次回答长度；0 不发送此限制，由服务决定。 上下文长度 配置模型的上下文预算，过长对话从最旧消息开始裁剪；0 表示未知、不按此设置裁剪。 代理与 TLS 配置代理地址，或按连接设置跳过 TLS 证书验证；正常证书连接保留验证。 自定义请求头 为网关附加请求头，值加密保存；编辑时不会返回已保存的明文。 自定义参数 JSON 附加服务参数，不能覆盖 model、messages、tools、stream 等平台管理字段。 “测试连接”使用当前表单中的地址、模型和高级设置；编辑时可复用已保存的密钥。通过后再保存，检查默认状态是否符合预期。 凭据与权限 密钥和自定义请求头值加密保存，不以明文返回列表或编辑表单。连接管理权限与聊天权限分开授予，能聊天不代表可以编辑模型连接。 系统参数中仅保留助手总开关 assistant.enabled 。模型地址、密钥与限额在 LLM 管理维护；旧版参数会在显式数据库迁移时转入连接记录。 接入后检查 测试连接，确认模型标识与密钥有效。 启用并设为默认，打开助手提出需要查询平台数据的问题。 检查工具读取与回答，确认服务兼容工具调用。 为有不同需要的 Skill 或定时任务指定其他已启用模型。

title: AI 定时任务与邮件
summary: 按计划查询平台，把模型回答保存并通过邮件发送。
text: 按计划提问并发送回答 AI 定时任务由提示词、运行计划、收件人、回答语言和可选 LLM 组成。平台到点后调用模型，模型使用与聊天相同的平台查询工具，回答保存为运行记录并通过邮件发送。可用于每日状态摘要、每周模块效果分析或定期检查降级情况。 任务不会自动修改资源或参数。运行结果取决于提示词、可用记录与所选模型；配置的定时提问也不会替代持续告警规则。 创建任务 聊天中可以说：“每周一早上 9 点把所有模块的使用状态发到我的邮箱。”助手创建后会说明计划与下次时间。当前用户必须有身份和有效邮箱；聊天创建的任务只发给本人，提示词中指定其他收件人不会改变这一点。 使用 /tasks 查看自己的任务。管理员可在“AI 配置 → 定时任务”管理全部任务，新增或修改提示词、计划、收件人、语言、启用状态与模型，也可立即运行并查看各次回答。 计划与时区 计划按平台时区解释，默认 UTC+8；下面示例均按 UTC+8。最短间隔为 1 小时，每个用户最多 20 个任务，提示词最长 2000 字符。 计划 含义 0 9 * * 1 每周一 09:00。 0 8 * * * 每天 08:00。 0 9 1 * * 每月 1 日 09:00。 @every 24h 按 24 小时间隔执行，不等同于固定每天某个钟点。 保存前确认界面的下次运行时间。停机期间遗漏的历史时刻不会逐次补跑；恢复后到期任务执行一次，再推进到后续计划。上一次运行未结束时跳过下一次，避免重叠。 配置邮件渠道 在“系统管理 → 系统参数”的通知分类配置 SMTP。任务使用平台通知渠道发送，必须先配置可用的发件服务器。 参数 含义 notify.email.host / port SMTP 服务器与端口。 notify.email.security starttls 、 tls 或 none ，与邮件服务要求一致。 notify.email.username / password 登录账户与密码，密码加密保存并遮盖显示。 notify.email.from 发件地址。 notify.email.skip_verify 是否跳过服务端证书验证。 notify.email.timeout_seconds 邮件连接与发送的超时。 带密码的认证只在加密连接或本机连接上发送。任务回答是 HTML（在提示词里要求模型输出 HTML 邮件）时，邮件同时带 HTML 与纯文本两个版本；否则是纯文本，Markdown 按文本保留。发信服务器的填法、加密方式和常见错误见 邮件（SMTP）配置 。 运行记录与重试 运行进入任务中心，可查看回答、模型读取的工具、收件人与发送结果。失败可重试；已有回答会复用，不重复询问模型，已经发送成功的收件人不会因同次作业重试再次收到邮件。 没有收到邮件时，依次检查：任务启用与下次时间、默认或指定模型、任务中心运行错误、SMTP 配置和收件地址。没有配置模型或邮件渠道时，查看明确错误后先完成配置。

title: 首页与运行概览
summary: 查看模块状态、需要关注的模块和实际扩缩容活动。
text: 首页查看平台运行情况 有首页权限时，登录后进入运行概览。统一时间范围下查看已启用与全部模块、运行模式分布、需要关注的模块、已执行扩缩容及失败运行，再进入对应模块处理。 需要关注的模块 标记 检查方向 连续失败 连续失败至少 3 次，查看最近错误、数据源与算法运行。 推荐降级 检查采用来源与兜底原因。 推荐过期 检查任务调度、预测与决策刷新。 没有推荐 应生成推荐却尚未产生，检查模块与指标配置。 已旁路 确认是否为计划中的人工接管。 仅观察或未启用预测的模块，不会只因没有推荐就被标记为异常。旁路也不一定是故障，应结合操作原因判断。 看清执行与效果 扩缩容图按时间段累计 Operator 已成功执行的动作，不把预测建议当作实际动作；没有执行的时段显示 0。从关注列表打开“效果报告”，继续查看准确度、扩容及时性、容量与稳定性。 首页读取已有状态，不主动触发预测、执行或修复。更详细排查见 监控与问题排查 ，自然语言查询见 AI 助手 。

title: 监控与问题排查
summary: 从数据源、算法运行到实际副本，定位流程中的异常。
text: 按流程定位问题 现象 优先检查 没有历史数据 数据源连接、模板变量、标签、查询时间范围和单位。 部分算法没有结果 算法运行情况中的最小样本、参数、输入和耗时。 评估暂时为空 预测目标时间是否到达，实际指标是否已采集。 推荐使用兜底 快照中的来源、数据新鲜度、算法资格与恢复状态。 副本没有变化 模式授权、旁路、控制冲突、建议有效期、步长和冷却。 目标已写入但容量不足 实际副本、Ready、Pod 启动与资源准备时间。 查看指标与曲线 使用指标目录与查询查看历史用量、预测、实际表现、推荐新鲜度和运行状态。缺失位置应与真实采样区分，不能把跨缺口的连接线解释为实测值。 接入外部监控 配置 metrics.listen 后，平台提供 /metrics 、 /healthz 和 /readyz 。平台指标使用 kube_res_foresight_* ，Operator 指标使用 kube_res_foresight_operator_* 。 指标用于观察链路，不替代推荐快照、执行报告或实际就绪状态。同步准入不等待 Prometheus 长查询或模型推理。 结合记录复盘 从模块定位算法运行、预测、资源评估、推荐、准入和执行。需要离线核对时使用审计导出，并确认导出时间范围和权限。 观察决策来源与扩容延迟 平台正常响应、缓存接管、恢复中和缓存过期是不同状态。通过 kube_res_foresight_operator_decision_source_total 与 kube_res_foresight_operator_decision_cache_age_seconds 观察决策来源与缓存年龄，再结合扩容及时性和 Ready 曲线排查预测落后或容量就绪偏慢。 预测关闭时没有算法结果属于预期状态。排查前先检查模块预测方式，再查看数据、模型和执行链路。

title: 平台管理
summary: 维护权限、任务、审计和时区，支持日常运行与复盘。
text: 用户、角色与权限 通过用户、角色、菜单和 API 权限分配访问范围。区分查看结果、修改策略和授权执行，机器凭据按用途配置最小权限。 目录认证 在系统管理 → 系统参数的 LDAP 分类中配置连接、用户和组查询、角色映射、连接检查与同步。支持 LDAPS / StartTLS 配置；本地账号保留本地认证，作为目录不可用时的应急入口。参数、角色映射和排查见 LDAP 登录配置 。 任务与全局设置 任务中心管理周期任务、调度和执行记录。失败后先核对输入与错误，再处理重试。全局参数维护安全开关、前瞻决策和默认配置，模块负责各工作负载自己的边界与策略。 存储与显示时区 时间存储使用 UTC。平台默认时区为 UTC+8，可通过 KUBE_RES_FORESIGHT_TIMEZONE 配置，作用于日志、数据库会话与新模块周期；页面固定按 UTC+8 显示，不跟随浏览器时区。调度区间仍按显式 IANA 时区解释。 日志、保留与导出 登录日志记录认证行为，操作日志记录配置和导出等操作。推荐、执行、准入和降级记录帮助解释资源变化。按复盘周期设置保留要求，备份数据库及稳定的凭据加密密钥。 控制历史保留与准入记录量 通过系统参数 forecast.history_retention_days 统一配置历史保留天数；默认 0 使用各类记录内置保留周期。 forecast.evaluation_max_per_module 默认每模块保留最新 20,000 条实测评估，最少 100 条。 准入调用需携带 request_uid 才生成记录，并按 UID 去重。具备工作负载版本信息时，默认记录创建及每个新版本的首个 Pod；扩容和替换产生的后续 Pod 仍正常处理，但不逐一记录。需要完整记录时启用 forecast.admission_record_scaling 。有请求 UID、没有版本信息时继续逐次记录。 AI 配置与通知 系统参数 assistant.enabled 控制聊天入口；“AI 配置”分别管理 LLM 连接 、 Skill 与 定时任务 。LLM、Skill、任务菜单和 assistant:chat 权限分别授予。 邮件使用系统参数通知分类的 notify.email.* 配置，填法见 邮件（SMTP）配置 。接入前同时检查模型连接、邮箱与 SMTP，定时任务运行结果在任务中心与任务记录中查看。

title: LDAP 登录配置
summary: 配置目录登录、取组方式和角色映射，并沿用其他系统已有的 LDAP 设置。
text: 登录怎么判断本地还是目录用户 登录页没有“来源”选项，平台按用户名在本地库里的情况决定： 情况 处理 本地库有这个用户名，来源是本地 只校验本地密码，不访问目录。 admin 因此在目录不可用时仍能登录。 本地库有，来源是 LDAP 只向目录校验密码。 本地库没有，LDAP 已启用 向目录认证；通过后按角色映射得出角色，并自动创建 LDAP 用户。 本地库没有，LDAP 未启用 登录失败。 目录里与本地账号同名的用户不会接管本地账号。LDAP 用户在本地的密码是随机值，无法用于本地登录，也不能在个人中心修改密码，请在目录中修改。用户列表和个人中心会显示账号来源。 参数 在“系统管理 → 系统参数”的 LDAP 分类里逐项设置，每项单独保存。 参数 含义 ldap.url 目录地址，如 ldaps://ldap.example.com:636 。使用 ldap:// 时必须开启 StartTLS。 ldap.start_tls / ldap.skip_verify StartTLS；是否跳过证书校验。能提供 CA 时不要跳过。 ldap.ca_cert 自签名证书的 CA（PEM）。保存后只显示掩码。 ldap.bind_dn / ldap.bind_password 用于查询用户的服务账号。密码加密保存，必须先设置 bind DN。 ldap.user_base_dn 搜索用户的起点，如 dc=example,dc=com 。 ldap.user_filter 查找用户的过滤器，必须恰好含一个 %s （登录名），如 (cn=%s) 或 (&(objectClass=person)(uid=%s)) 。 ldap.display_name_attr / email_attr / phone_attr 显示名、邮箱、电话对应的属性，每次登录刷新。 ldap.member_of_attr 用户条目上列出所属组 DN 的属性，通常是 memberOf 。设置后直接读取它取组。 ldap.group_base_dn / ldap.group_filter 不使用 memberOf 时，到组条目里查成员：过滤器里 %s 是用户 DN， %u 是登录名，如 (member=%s) 。两项要一起有或一起空：设置其中一项而另一项为空时会自动补上常用值，清空其中一项会一起清空。 ldap.group_name_attr 组条目里作为组名的属性，默认 cn 。 ldap.group_role_mappings 组到角色的映射，见下节。 ldap.default_role_code 不在任何映射组里的用户使用的角色。留空则这些用户无法登录。 ldap.timeout_seconds 连接和查询超时，1 到 120 秒。 ldap.enabled 是否启用目录登录。 启用时平台会校验整套配置并连接目录检查一次，不通过就拒绝启用并说明原因，所以请把 ldap.enabled 放在最后设置。 取组的两种方式 二选一，也可以同时使用，结果合并。 读用户的 memberOf ：设置 ldap.member_of_attr ，不需要组基础 DN 和过滤器。每个值（组的 DN）既可以按完整 DN 匹配，也可以按 DN 第一段的值匹配（ cn=ops,ou=groups,… 对应 ops ）。 到组条目里查成员 ：设置 ldap.group_base_dn 、 ldap.group_filter ，用 ldap.group_name_attr 取组名。常见写法：OpenLDAP 的 groupOfNames 用 (member=%s) ；posixGroup 用 (memberUid=%u) ；AD 需要包含嵌套组时用 (member:1.2.840.113556.1.4.1941:=%s) 。 角色映射 ldap.group_role_mappings 每行一条，格式为 组=角色编码 ： ops=ADMIN dev=VIEWER ou=sre,ou=平台组,dc=example,dc=com=ADMIN 左边是组名（ cn ）或完整 DN，不区分大小写；完整 DN 里的空格要与目录返回的一致。 右边是角色的 编码 ，在“授权管理 → 角色”里查看。角色必须存在并已启用。 程序按最后一个 = 切分，所以完整 DN 的写法可以直接用。一个组可以写多行授予多个角色。用户属于多个组时取角色的并集。 以 # 开头的行是注释，空行忽略。格式不对或重复的行在保存时被拒绝。 用户不在任何映射组里时使用 ldap.default_role_code ；两者都没有就拒绝登录。已存在的 LDAP 用户如果失去所有角色，会被停用并结束其会话。 沿用已有的 LDAP 配置 公司里其他系统（Wiki、代码仓库、监控、CI 等）通常已经接入了同一个目录，它们的 LDAP 设置里已有这里需要的信息。照下表把已有的值填到对应参数即可： 已有的信息 填到 服务器地址、端口、是否 SSL ldap.url ，SSL 写成 ldaps://地址:端口 是否 StartTLS、是否跳过证书校验 ldap.start_tls 、 ldap.skip_verify 查询用的账号（Bind DN）和密码 ldap.bind_dn 、 ldap.bind_password 用户搜索范围（Base DN） ldap.user_base_dn 用户搜索过滤器，其中登录名的占位符 ldap.user_filter ，占位符统一写成 %s 。例如 (cn=${username}) 、 (uid={0}) 、 (sAMAccountName=%(user)s) 都写成 (cn=%s) 这类形式 姓名、邮箱的属性名 ldap.display_name_attr 、 ldap.email_attr 用户条目里记录所属组的属性（常叫 memberOf） ldap.member_of_attr 组的搜索范围和成员过滤器（没有 memberOf 时） ldap.group_base_dn 、 ldap.group_filter “组的 DN → 角色/权限”的对应表 ldap.group_role_mappings ，每条写成 组 DN=本平台的角色编码 其他系统里的角色（管理员、编辑、只读等）和本平台的角色没有固定对应，请改用你在“授权管理 → 角色”里建好的角色编码。平台自带的管理员角色编码是 ADMIN ，拥有全部权限，授予整个组之前先确认。 完整配置示例与一次登录的过程 下面用两个常见目录，把每个参数具体填什么、一次登录里平台做了什么，放在一起看。地址、DN 和组名都是示例，请换成你们目录里的值。 示例一：OpenLDAP，用组条目里的成员关系取组 目录里有： LDIF 复制 dn: uid=alice,ou=people,dc=example,dc=com uid: alice cn: Alice Zhang mail: alice@example.com dn: cn=sre,ou=groups,dc=example,dc=com objectClass: groupOfNames cn: sre member: uid=alice,ou=people,dc=example,dc=com 系统参数这样填（“系统管理 → 系统参数 → LDAP 认证”，每项单独保存，最后再启用）： 参数 值 说明 ldap.url ldaps://ldap.example.com:636 用 LDAPS；如果用 ldap:// ，必须开 StartTLS。 ldap.bind_dn cn=readonly,dc=example,dc=com 只读的服务账号，用来搜索用户。 ldap.bind_password 服务账号的密码 加密保存。 ldap.user_base_dn ou=people,dc=example,dc=com 从这里往下搜索用户。 ldap.user_filter (uid=%s) %s 会被替换成登录名。 ldap.display_name_attr cn 显示名。 ldap.email_attr mail 邮箱。 ldap.group_base_dn ou=groups,dc=example,dc=com 到这里搜索组条目。 ldap.group_filter (member=%s) 这里的 %s 是 用户的 DN ，不是登录名。 ldap.group_name_attr cn （默认） 组条目里作为组名的属性。 ldap.group_role_mappings sre=ADMIN dev=VIEWER 每行 组=角色编码 。 ldap.default_role_code 留空 不在映射组里的人无法登录。想让他们以只读登录，填一个只读角色的编码。 ldap.enabled true 最后设置：启用时平台会校验整套配置并连一次目录。 alice 登录时发生了什么： 平台用 LDAPS 连接目录，并用服务账号 cn=readonly,… 登录。 在 ou=people,… 下用 (uid=alice) 搜索。找到一条 uid=alice,ou=people,dc=example,dc=com ；一条也没有是“用户不存在”，多于一条会被拒绝（过滤器必须只匹配一个人）。输入的登录名里的特殊字符会被转义，不能用来改写过滤器。 用这个 DN 和 alice 输入的密码再登录一次。 密码只由目录校验 ，平台不保存也不比较。 读取 cn 和 mail ，得到显示名 Alice Zhang 和邮箱。 取组：在 ou=groups,… 下用 (member=uid=alice,ou=people,dc=example,dc=com) 搜索，找到组 cn=sre ，组名是 sre 。 按角色映射 sre=ADMIN ，alice 得到 ADMIN 角色；本地库里没有 alice，所以自动创建一个来源为 LDAP 的用户并登录。 示例二：Active Directory，直接读 memberOf 参数 值 ldap.url ldaps://ad.example.com:636 ldap.bind_dn CN=svc-krf,OU=Service Accounts,DC=example,DC=com ldap.user_base_dn DC=example,DC=com ldap.user_filter (&(objectClass=user)(sAMAccountName=%s)) ldap.display_name_attr / ldap.email_attr displayName / mail ldap.member_of_attr memberOf ldap.group_base_dn / ldap.group_filter 留空（用 memberOf 就不需要） ldap.group_role_mappings Platform-Admins=ADMIN CN=Platform-Readers,OU=Groups,DC=example,DC=com=VIEWER AD 用户条目的 memberOf 里是每个组的完整 DN，例如 CN=Platform-Admins,OU=Groups,DC=example,DC=com 。映射左边既可以写完整 DN，也可以只写第一段的值（ Platform-Admins ），平台两种都会匹配。第二行展示了完整 DN 的写法：程序按最后一个 = 切分，前面的整个 DN 不受影响。需要把嵌套组也算进来时，不用 memberOf ，改用组过滤器 (member:1.2.840.113556.1.4.1941:=%s) 。 启用前先自查 服务账号能搜到用户：用任何 LDAP 客户端以它登录，对 user_base_dn 用同样的过滤器查一个已知用户，应当恰好返回一条。 角色编码存在且已启用：映射右边的编码要和“授权管理 → 角色”里的一致。 先试普通用户再试管理员：确认映射的角色不会把不该有的权限给了整个组。 同步与停用 目录里被删除、被禁用或不再属于任何映射组的用户，会在同步时被停用并结束会话；目录重新启用的用户会恢复，被管理员手动停用的除外。目录不可达时不会改动任何账号，避免一次故障把所有人锁在外面。 排查 现象 检查 无法启用，提示目录检查失败 地址和端口、证书（自签名需要 CA 或暂时跳过校验）、服务账号和密码、网络是否通。 登录失败，页面只显示用户名或密码错误 看平台日志中的 ldap login refused ， reason 写明具体原因。 the user belongs to no group mapped to a role 认证已通过，但没有角色。括号里的 groups found 是目录返回的组：为空说明取组方式或过滤器不对；有组名则补映射或设置默认角色。 a local account with this name exists 本地已有同名账号，目录不会接管它；改用本地密码，或让管理员处理这个账号。 某一项保存被拒绝 启用状态下每次修改都会校验整套配置。必填项（地址、用户基础 DN、用户过滤器）不能留空；bind DN 与密码要成对。 本地账号始终可以用本地密码登录，目录不可用不影响它们。

title: 邮件（SMTP）配置
summary: 配置发信服务器、加密方式和发件地址，按常见邮件服务填写，先发测试邮件再排查错误。
text: 邮件通道是什么，谁在用 邮件通道让平台通过一台 SMTP 服务器给指定邮箱发信。目前用它的是 AI 定时任务 ：任务按计划让模型回答，再把回答发给收件人。通道本身只管“把一封信交给 SMTP 服务器”，不管内容；没有配置好时，任务运行会失败并在任务中心写明原因，不会静默丢信。 配置全部在“系统管理 → 系统参数”的 通知 分类里，没有配置文件。每一项单独保存，刚保存的参数最多 10 秒后生效。配好后用同一页的“发送测试邮件”按钮给自己发一封，是最快的验证办法。 参数 参数 默认值 含义 notify.email.host 空 SMTP 服务器主机名或 IP。为空表示邮件通道没有配置，发送会直接失败。 notify.email.port 587 端口，1 到 65535。常见搭配：587 + starttls ，465 + tls ，25 + none 。 notify.email.security starttls 连接加密方式： starttls （先明文连接再升级为加密）、 tls （整条连接一开始就是 TLS，也叫隐式 TLS / SMTPS）、 none （不加密）。 notify.email.username 空 登录 SMTP 服务器的账号。服务器不需要登录时留空。 notify.email.password 空 账号的密码或应用专用密码。加密保存，保存后只显示掩码；提交掩码表示保持原值。 notify.email.from 空 发件地址，必填。可以写 reports@example.com ，也可以写带显示名的 "kube-res-foresight <reports@example.com>" 。邮件服务通常要求它与登录账号一致或是该账号有权代发的地址。 notify.email.skip_verify false 是否跳过服务器证书校验。服务器用自签名证书时才临时打开；打开后连接可能被冒充，能提供受信任证书时不要开。 notify.email.timeout_seconds 30 一封邮件从连接、登录到交付给服务器的总时限，5 到 300 秒。 “启用”没有单独的开关： host 、 port 、 from 都有效，通道就可用。 加密与密码：什么时候会发送登录密码 平台使用标准的 SMTP PLAIN 登录。出于安全， 账号密码只会在加密连接上发送 ，或者发给本机上的服务器；在一条不加密的外部连接上，登录会被拒绝，而不是把密码明文发出去。 security 典型端口 过程 能否带账号密码 starttls 587 先用明文连上并问候，服务器必须声明支持 STARTTLS，然后升级为 TLS，再登录和发信。服务器不支持时报错而不是退回明文。 可以（升级之后） tls 465 一开始就建立 TLS，之后登录和发信。 可以 none 25 全程不加密。 只有服务器在本机时可以；用于内网无认证的中继。 常见邮件服务的填法 下面的主机名、地址和密码都是示例，请换成你自己的。具体要求以邮件服务商的说明为准（有的需要“应用专用密码”或在管理后台允许 SMTP 登录）。 企业邮箱 / Microsoft 365 一类的 587 + STARTTLS 参数 值 notify.email.host smtp.example.com notify.email.port 587 notify.email.security starttls notify.email.username reports@example.com notify.email.password 该账号的密码或应用专用密码 notify.email.from kube-res-foresight <reports@example.com> 465 + 隐式 TLS（一些国内邮箱服务） 与上表相同，只把 port 改成 465 、 security 改成 tls 。 内网中继，不登录 参数 值 notify.email.host mail-relay.internal notify.email.port 25 notify.email.security none notify.email.username / password 留空 notify.email.from reports@example.com （中继允许的发件地址） 这种配置信件内容在内网里是明文传输的，只适合受信任的网络。 自签名证书的内部服务器 先按服务器实际的端口和加密方式填，再把 notify.email.skip_verify 设为 true 。这只是权宜之计：证书不校验，连接可能被冒充；长期使用应给服务器换成受信任的证书。 发出的邮件长什么样 邮件内容用 UTF-8，经 base64 编码，中文主题也能正常显示。任务回答是 HTML 时，邮件同时带纯文本和 HTML 两个版本（multipart/alternative）：支持 HTML 的邮箱客户端显示带标题、表格和颜色的版本，其他客户端显示纯文本。平台会去掉 HTML 里的脚本、框架和对象，邮件客户端本来也不会显示它们。内容里的换行不会被用来构造邮件头。 一封邮件发给一个收件人；一个任务有多个收件人时分别发送，其中某个失败不会让已经发成功的重发。 先发一封测试邮件 “系统管理 → 系统参数”里，通知分类有“发送测试邮件”：填一个收件邮箱，平台用当前保存的参数发一封测试信。成功会提示已发送；失败时直接显示邮件服务器的原话，这是排查最有用的信息。刚改的参数最多 10 秒后生效，改完请稍等再测。 排查 提示（节选） 原因与检查 the e-mail channel is not set up: the SMTP host (notify.email.host) is empty 没有填主机。 the SMTP port (notify.email.port) is not valid 端口不在 1 到 65535。 the sender address (notify.email.from) is not set / is not valid 发件地址为空或格式不对；带显示名时要写成 名称 <地址> 。 the security (notify.email.security) is starttls, tls or none security 只能是这三个值之一。 could not reach the SMTP server host:port 连不上：主机名、端口、防火墙或出站网络策略。容器里要确认平台所在的 Pod 能访问该地址。 the SMTP server did not greet 连上了但服务器没有按 SMTP 问候，常见于端口与加密方式不匹配，例如在 465 上用了 starttls ，应改成 tls 。 the SMTP server does not offer STARTTLS 服务器不支持升级加密：换成它支持的方式（ tls ），或确认是不加密的内网中继再用 none 。 STARTTLS failed / 证书相关错误 证书不被信任或域名不匹配。检查服务器证书；自签名证书可临时开 skip_verify 。 the SMTP server refused the sign-in 账号或密码不对，或服务器要求应用专用密码、没有允许该账号用 SMTP 登录。 the SMTP server refused the sender 发件地址不被允许：通常要与登录账号一致，或该账号有权代发。 the SMTP server refused the recipient … 收件地址被拒绝：地址错误，或服务器不允许向外部域发信（中继限制）。 任务运行失败时，错误也会出现在任务中心的运行记录里，已经发送成功的收件人不会因为重试再收到一次。

title: 常见问题
summary: 查找接入、算法选择、执行模式和资源更新的常见答案。
text: 官网可以直接管理集群吗？ 官网提供项目介绍和使用指南。管理平台需要独立部署，用于连接数据源、配置模块、查看建议和授权执行。 应该选择哪个算法？ 先从基线开始，在相同历史窗口和预测视野下比较资源误差、峰值低估和耗时。算法复杂度不能替代业务表现；可用预测还能参与共识决策。 可以与 HPA 或 KEDA 同时使用吗？ 可以分别管理不同工作负载，但不能同时控制同一目标的副本。切换前先停止旧控制器并释放控制权。 为什么没有预测或评分？ 先检查模块是否启用预测，以及是否选择了“不预测”。新建模块默认关闭预测，使用兜底默认值属于主动配置，不算算法故障。开启后再检查数据源、模板标签、单位、历史样本、算法运行和预测新鲜度。实测评分需要等待预测目标时间到达，并成功采集对应实际值。 推荐变化后，运行中的 Pod 会立即更新吗？ 资源准入作用于新 Pod，运行中的配置通过新建或滚动更新应用。副本伸缩是独立动作，由 Operator 按有效建议执行。 如何暂停自动化？ 启用模块旁路或关闭对应全局开关，回到观察或推荐。检查实际资源状态后再决定是否恢复先前配置，旁路不会自动撤销已经发生的变化。

title: Documentation
summary: Understand the capabilities, connect your metrics, and manage resources. Find the guide for your next step.
text: New to the project? Start with a quick walkthrough or explore the core concepts first. Start reading → Getting started Quick start Connect a workload and follow your first recommendation. Installation Prepare the platform, job engine, and optional execution components. Core concepts System architecture Explore the overview, module responsibilities, and execution paths. Runtime and feedback loops Understand collection, forecasts, advice, refresh, and actual outcomes. Capabilities and concepts Understand modules, metric templates, models, and operating policies. Metrics and data quality Connect sources, templates, and datasets to prepare dependable inputs. Models and prediction modes Choose fixed or dynamic methods, explore models, corrections, and eligibility. Algorithm reference Naive Repeats the latest observation across the horizon. Use it as a basic comparison and to check the data workflow; it cannot anticipate cycles or sudden changes. Seasonal Naive Repeats the corresponding observations from the preceding cycle. A seasonal baseline for repeating demand; anomalies in that cycle are repeated too. EWMA Smooths recent observations and projects the resulting level. A low-cost candidate for recent demand, without explicit daily seasonality. Damped Trend Estimates where a slow climb that has begun is heading from the newest stretch of history, with a slope that fades so the forecast converges to a ceiling. Suits memory and caches that creep up with sudden drops. Histogram Percentile Uses a time-decayed historical percentile as a constant future level. Useful for comparing high-water resource sizing, without predicting when a peak occurs. Random Forest Fits and averages regression trees on sampled historical features, supporting nonlinear relationships and covariates. More costly than simple statistical methods. KNN Finds similar historical windows and follows their subsequent trajectories. Useful for recurring shapes, with limited ability to anticipate patterns absent from history. Holt-Winters Models level, trend, and seasonality with additive or multiplicative seasons and optional damped trend. Suitable for cyclic demand with changing levels. Model service · forecasting and tuning Calls an external time-series model over HTTP. Configure it in Model management, then choose the module prediction mode. A failed request fails that candidate while other eligible methods continue. Theta Combines a smoothed level with half the fitted linear slope, optionally removing seasonality first. A candidate for noisy trends; forecasts are clamped at zero. MSTL Separates daily and weekly seasonal shapes and applies Theta to the remainder. This implementation iterates fixed seasonal shapes rather than time-varying LOESS components. Seasonal Profile Groups observations by time of day and optionally weekday, then uses a decayed percentile per bucket. Useful for weekday/weekend demand patterns. Peak Envelope Builds a rolling-maximum envelope and extrapolates its robust slope. Targets high-water demand rather than averages, such as memory sawtooth patterns and cache growth. Combination Combines member forecasts using a stepwise median or recent-error weights. The combination must earn backtest promotion like other candidates. Ridge AR Fits linear relationships from lags, optional UTC calendar features, and covariates. A relatively inexpensive machine-learning candidate for stable linear dependencies. GBDT Fits successive trees to residuals using lags, calendars, and covariates. Supports squared-error point forecasts or a native quantile objective. User guides Backtesting and evaluation Compare resource forecasts with actual use and understand scores and rankings. Recommendations and look-ahead Learn how model consensus, lead time, and constraints shape resource advice. Admission and scaling Enable Pod resource advice and replica scaling separately, then review outcomes. Safety and fallback Manage schedules, fallback, bypass, and safeguards for automatic actions. AI assistant AI assistant and skills Query platform state, use slash commands, export reports, and explain changes. LLM configuration Configure default and selected models, tools, advanced settings, and credentials. AI scheduled tasks and email Ask on a schedule, retain answers, and deliver them by email. Operations Dashboard and activity Review module status, attention flags, and applied scaling activity. Monitoring and troubleshooting Trace issues from data sources and model runs to actual replica readiness. Administration Manage access, scheduled tasks, audit, and time settings. LDAP sign-in Set up directory login, how groups are read, and role mapping, and reuse the LDAP settings other systems already have. Email (SMTP) setup Set the mail server, the encryption and the sender, fill it in for common mail services, send a test mail first and read the errors. Common questions Find answers about setup, model choice, operating modes, and resource updates.

title: Quick start
summary: Connect a workload and follow your first recommendation.
text: Start with one workload Connect a noncritical workload to your own metrics. Begin with observation, review the advice, and gradually authorize actions. Add a source. Configure a Metrics data source and check the connection. Define metric templates. Choose CPU, memory, request volume, or other inputs. Confirm queries, units, and aggregation scope. Create a module. Select the namespace, workload, and container. Connect templates and configure intervals, bounds, schedules, and fallback. Run and compare. Inspect history quality, model predictions, backtests, actual performance, and recommendations. What to review first Area What to check History and datasets Scope, units, sample interval, gaps, and freshness. Model runs Successful runs and reasons for insufficient history, missing parameters, or timeout. Backtests and evaluation CPU and memory forecast errors, particularly peak underestimation. Recommendation details Resource and replica advice, constraints, consensus, expiry, and fallback reasons. Enable automation gradually Start in Observe and review advice in Recommend . Authorize Admission and Auto separately when ready to apply changes. Both write paths are disabled by global settings by default. Review before acting Confirm metric meaning, sufficient history, explainable advice, appropriate bounds, and fallback values. Review admission and replica scaling separately. Move from collection to model forecasts Confirm history collection first, then enable prediction. Choose Dynamic algorithms to compare methods, or Fixed algorithm and select a specific method. Non-baseline models need backtest promotion before their results can be adopted. Fallback defaults are expected while prediction is disabled or No prediction is selected. Stay in Observe or Recommend while reviewing forecasts, scores, and look-ahead details. Authorize admission or scaling separately. See prediction modes .

title: Installation
summary: Prepare the platform, job engine, and optional execution components.
text: Choose the components The platform provides the console, data management, forecasting, and advice. The job engine runs recurring work. Add the Operator for replica changes and admission policies for resource advice on new Pods. Component Purpose Platform Console, API, metrics, forecasts, and recommendations. Job engine Recurring collection, forecasts, backtests, and evaluations; can run with the platform. Operator Adjust workload replicas within authorization and bounds. Resource admission Apply valid resource advice to new Pod requests / limits. Deploy the platform with Helm Run these commands from the repository root with Helm 3, access to Kubernetes, and an image registry. Platform and Operator have separate charts. The platform chart runs the console, API, forecasting, and job engine; it does not install a database or the Operator. Prepare the separate web/ sources, then build and push the platform image. Replace the example registry and tag. Bash Copy docker build -f deploy/docker/Dockerfile --target kube-res-foresight \ -t registry.example.com/kube-res-foresight:0.1.0 . docker push registry.example.com/kube-res-foresight:0.1.0 For a trial, the defaults use SQLite and a 5Gi PVC. A working StorageClass is required. SQLite permits only one platform replica. Bash Copy helm install kube-res-foresight deploy/helm/kube-res-foresight \ -n kube-res-foresight --create-namespace \ --set image.repository=registry.example.com/kube-res-foresight \ --set image.tag=0.1.0 Database and secrets For external PostgreSQL or MySQL, create a database and a user allowed to create tables, then prepare a credentials Secret. The platform does not provision a database server. This is an alternative installation; do not run it after the SQLite example. Bash Copy kubectl create namespace kube-res-foresight kubectl -n kube-res-foresight create secret generic kube-res-foresight-credentials \ --from-file=jwt-secret=./jwt-secret.txt \ --from-file=secret-key=./secret-key.txt \ --from-file=database-password=./database-password.txt The files contain the JWT signing key, an encryption key of at least 32 characters, and the database password, respectively, with no trailing newline. Protect these files and keep them out of version control. Create values-production.yaml : YAML Copy image: repository: registry.example.com/kube-res-foresight tag: "0.1.0" database: driver: postgres host: pg.example.internal port: 5432 name: kube-res-foresight username: kube-res-foresight sslMode: require secrets: existingSecret: kube-res-foresight-credentials persistence: enabled: false Bash Copy helm install kube-res-foresight deploy/helm/kube-res-foresight \ -n kube-res-foresight -f values-production.yaml kubectl -n kube-res-foresight rollout status deployment/kube-res-foresight helm test kube-res-foresight -n kube-res-foresight kubectl -n kube-res-foresight port-forward svc/kube-res-foresight 8080:80 Open http://localhost:8080 . The initial login is admin / 123456 ; change the password immediately. For MySQL, use database.driver: mysql , port 3306 , and the corresponding connection settings. sslMode applies only to PostgreSQL; this example requires TLS support on the server. Value Purpose migration.mode: auto Defaults to an init container for SQLite and a pre-install/pre-upgrade hook Job for external databases. imagePullSecrets Credentials for pulling private images. ingress Controller class, host, and TLS; disabled by default. resources Platform container requests / limits; size for module count and history windows. secrets.existingSecret Reuse stable keys. Default keys: jwt-secret, secret-key, database-password. Manage mail, model connections, and prediction rules in the console. All deployment settings are listed in platform values.yaml ↗ . Deploy the Operator with Helm Create a platform developer credential restricted to Operator decision reading and reporting. Save access-key:access-secret in operator-credential.txt without a trailing newline, then create its Secret. The platform chart does not create this credential. Bash Copy docker build -f deploy/docker/Dockerfile --target operator \ -t registry.example.com/kube-res-foresight-operator:0.1.0 . docker push registry.example.com/kube-res-foresight-operator:0.1.0 kubectl -n kube-res-foresight create secret generic kube-res-foresight-platform \ --from-file=credential=./operator-credential.txt helm install kube-res-foresight-operator deploy/helm/kube-res-foresight-operator \ -n kube-res-foresight \ --set image.repository=registry.example.com/kube-res-foresight-operator \ --set image.tag=0.1.0 \ --set platform.url=http://kube-res-foresight.kube-res-foresight.svc \ --set platform.credentialSecret.name=kube-res-foresight-platform kubectl -n kube-res-foresight rollout status deployment/kube-res-foresight-operator The Operator defaults to two replicas with leader election and needs no CRD. Configure workloads and scaling rules through platform modules. Check that HPA/KEDA does not control the same target before enabling the global auto-mode setting and module Auto mode. Configure Kyverno separately for new Pod resource admission. Prometheus and Grafana With the Prometheus Operator CRDs installed, enable discovery, alert rules, and the Grafana dashboard ConfigMap. Replace the example release=prom selector label to match your Prometheus. Grafana needs a sidecar configured to load dashboard ConfigMaps. Bash Copy helm upgrade kube-res-foresight deploy/helm/kube-res-foresight \ -n kube-res-foresight --reuse-values \ --set metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled=true \ --set metrics.serviceMonitor.labels.release=prom \ --set metrics.prometheusRule.enabled=true \ --set metrics.prometheusRule.labels.release=prom \ --set metrics.grafanaDashboard.enabled=true helm upgrade kube-res-foresight-operator deploy/helm/kube-res-foresight-operator \ -n kube-res-foresight --reuse-values \ --set metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled=true \ --set metrics.serviceMonitor.labels.release=prom Helm upgrade and uninstall Back up the database before upgrading and keep the original Secret. Changing the encryption key prevents decryption of existing connection passwords. The chart runs regular migrations, not the retired-table cleanup performed by --upgrade . Bash Copy helm upgrade kube-res-foresight deploy/helm/kube-res-foresight \ -n kube-res-foresight --reuse-values --set image.tag=NEW_TAG helm upgrade kube-res-foresight-operator deploy/helm/kube-res-foresight-operator \ -n kube-res-foresight --reuse-values --set image.tag=NEW_TAG To remove the execution component and platform: Bash Copy helm uninstall kube-res-foresight-operator -n kube-res-foresight helm uninstall kube-res-foresight -n kube-res-foresight SQLite updates use Recreate with a brief interruption. Uninstall retains the chart-created platform Secret and SQLite PVC. External databases and user-created Secrets remain unchanged. Uninstalling the Operator leaves the workload replica counts it last wrote. Build the platform Use the Go, Node.js, and pnpm toolchains declared by the repository. The web/ frontend is a separate repository; prepare its sources before building. Bash Copy cd web pnpm install --frozen-lockfile cd .. make package-web mkdir -p target/bin go build -o target/bin/kube-res-foresight ./cmd Configure and start Set the database, listener, logging, and stable JWT key in config.yaml . Choose SQLite, MySQL, or PostgreSQL. Environment variables use KUBE_RES_FORESIGHT_ ; credentials use the encryption key KUBE_RES_FORESIGHT_SECRET_KEY . Bash Copy # First installation: explicit migration target/bin/kube-res-foresight server --config config.yaml --migration # Start the platform and job engine target/bin/kube-res-foresight all --config config.yaml The example port is 20001 . Open http://localhost:20001 after startup. The server and job commands can also run separately. Existing installations and execution Keep the existing database connection, path, and key values. Back up before upgrading and review the cleanup performed by --upgrade . Normal startup does not remove retired tables. Prepare cluster permissions, credentials, certificates, and policies for execution. Begin in Observe and review resource references and replica ownership before authorizing changes. Deployment guide ↗ · Operator installation ↗

title: System architecture
summary: Explore the overview, module responsibilities, and execution paths.
text: System overview kube-res-foresight connects collection, forecasting, recommendations, and controlled actions for one Kubernetes cluster. Follow blue data relationships to see how advice is produced, then green control relationships to see where it is applied. System overview Zoom out Zoom in Fit width Full screen 100% Open SVG ↗ System overview Metrics, the platform, advice, execution, and observed feedback. Boxes represent responsibilities, not necessarily separate deployments. Administration and audit Manage users, LDAP, permissions, connections, and settings; inspect actions, admissions, and degradation. Managed configuration and operation history. The console manages these capabilities through Platform APIs. Platform and task entry points share business rules and a database and can be combined according to deployment needs. Logical modules do not require separate services. Two independent execution paths Resource and replica execution Zoom out Zoom in Fit width Full screen 100% Open SVG ↗ Resource and replica execution Admission configures new Pods; the Operator separately controls replicas. Validated snapshot Freshness · version · authorization Path 1 · resources of new Pods Path 2 · workload replicas Pod creation admission request Kubernetes API Server Kyverno queries resource advice Snapshot only, no model inference Apply requests / limits Subject to module policy Operator reads advice Platform provides target replicas Check execution rules Bounds · readiness · cooldown · step Write replicas through Scale API One replica controller Kubernetes outcomes Pod resources and Ready capacity Invalid advice preserves resources Outages use cache and recovery rules Authorize admission and scaling separately; no overlapping writes Arrows represent data or control relationships. New Pod resources: API Server admission invokes Kyverno, whose policy queries validated, unexpired resource advice and applies authorized requests and managed limits. Admission does not wait for collection, inference, or long queries. Unavailable advice preserves original resources. Workload replicas: the Operator reads modules and decisions from the platform, checks bounds, readiness, cooldown, and step limits, then writes replicas through the Kubernetes Scale API. It neither reads the platform database nor changes Pod requests/limits. Authorize the paths separately. Only one controller may write a workload's replicas; the Operator and HPA/KEDA cannot control the same target simultaneously. Updated recommendations do not immediately resize running Pods. Storage and external dependencies Component Purpose and boundary Prometheus Supplies workload and cluster metrics. The platform queries it without replacing the metric store. Relational database Choose SQLite, MySQL, or PostgreSQL to retain settings, collected data, jobs, predictions, recommendations, and audits. Time-series service, optional Provides external forecasts and, where supported, background tuning. Failures follow candidate and fallback rules. LLM and email, optional The assistant queries records; scheduled tasks generate and email answers without directly writing resource or replica changes. Kubernetes API Handles admission and replica changes. Permissions, workload state, and readiness affect actual outcomes. Feedback and observability Platform and Operator expose Prometheus metrics for monitoring, including with Grafana. title: Runtime and feedback loops
summary: Understand collection, forecasts, advice, refresh, and actual outcomes.
text: Three ongoing cycles Forecasting, evaluation, and decision refresh have different cadences. A module's interval controls new forecasts, evaluations wait for target times, and the Operator keeps asking what replicas should do now. Forecast and feedback cycles Zoom out Zoom in Fit width Full screen 100% Open SVG ↗ Forecast and feedback cycles Forecasting, actual-value evaluation, and on-demand refresh run separately. 1 · Forecast cycle · module schedule Collect History + current Forecast Methods + models Recommend Consensus and safeguards Save snapshot Sources and expiry 2 · Evaluation cycle · after actuals arrive Match actuals Align forecast target times Measure error Underestimate · coverage Score and rank Compare candidate quality Next decision Eligibility and credibility 3 · Decision refresh · follow load between forecasts Operator polls Read latest decision Refresh observations Reuse fresh predictions Recompute advice Load + saved forecasts Operator applies Check execution rules again Arrows represent data or control relationships. Zoom and scroll, or save the original SVG. The sample interval determines time per observation; the history window determines how far back a method sees; the horizon determines how far forward it predicts; cooldown limits action frequency. These are distinct settings. Observe mode stops at collection and forecasting without producing execution recommendations. What happens in a forecast cycle Select due modules. The task center checks enabled modules and respects individual run intervals. Prepare history. Render metric queries for the workload, query Prometheus, align units and grids, and record gaps and freshness. Forecast. Disabled or No prediction uses defaults. Fixed mode runs one selected method; dynamic mode runs centrally enabled methods. Insufficient-history and failed candidates record reasons. Produce advice. Eligible forecasts enter resource and replica calculations with schedules, bounds, look-ahead consensus, and safeguards. Store results. Save forecasts, run information, and versioned, expiring recommendations for views, admission, and the Operator. Observe mode performs no resource changes. Baselines remain eligible. Candidates need promotion for the corresponding version. Parameter changes can alter model identity, so previous promotion does not automatically qualify a new configuration. Why ask for replicas ahead of demand? New Pods take time to become available. The platform uses measured or configured readiness time, decision wait, and recent lateness allowance to establish a lead window, then combines the available methods' required replicas in that window. Scale-up considers demand within the lead window. Scale-down requires stronger agreement over the whole horizon and current demand fitting into fewer replicas. Observed load above forecasts and existing capacity may trigger emergency scale-up, still within replica ceilings. Follow load between forecasts When the Operator polls, the platform checks decision freshness. Refresh reuses fresh stored forecasts, collects current observations, and recomputes advice. Algorithms run again only when the forecasts themselves are also stale. Refresh is serialized per module. Requests wait for a configured period while background refresh may continue, letting later polls read the new version. Modules with individual intervals retain their own cadence. Advice does not immediately become capacity For example, a workload has four replicas and advice asks for ten. With a two-minute cooldown and a maximum increase of one, it may hold during cooldown and first move to five once execution is allowed. These are example settings, not universal defaults. The Operator also checks target, permissions, conflicts, readiness, and bounds. Emergency scale-up may bypass ordinary upward cooldown and step limits; scale-down never takes that path. Successful execution means settings were submitted, while Ready replicas establish available capacity. Where safeguards apply Mechanism Effect OOM score weighting When enabled, penalizes memory scores in underallocated evaluation windows, affecting comparison rather than directly lowering memory forecasts. OOM memory floor Uses recent OOM events and memory observations to prevent overly low advice. JVM heap pressure Contributes a replica constraint when configured with the necessary heap metrics. Data or model degradation Without eligible forecasts, follows schedules, fallback, or unchanged-value rules and records the chosen source. Platform outage The Operator uses cache, hold, degradation, and stable recovery states, distinct from an individual model failure. How outcomes inform the next cycle Once forecast target times arrive, actuals are aligned to compute resource error, peak underestimation, and coverage and update scores and rankings. Rolling backtests compare candidates with baselines for eligibility; actual-value evaluation explains predictions that have already occurred. Scale-up outcomes compare Ready replicas and later demand to assess timeliness. Evaluated readiness and lateness inform later lead windows. Effect reports summarize accuracy, stability, Pod-hours, and capacity SLO.

title: Capabilities and concepts
summary: Understand modules, metric templates, models, and operating policies.
text: Start from the workload A module describes a Kubernetes workload and its forecasting, resource, and execution policies. Metrics supply inputs, models predict change, and recommendations combine forecasts with constraints. Actual outcomes feed the next evaluation. Metrics → Forecast and compare → Recommend → Bounded actions → Actual outcomes Modules, metrics, and models Concept What it manages Workload module Target, templates, intervals, thresholds, bounds, mode, and fallback. Metric template Queries, variables, meaning, units, and scope, rendered for each module. Dataset Sampling, aggregation, conversion, precision, and gap handling. Model Central activation, parameters, weights, budgets, and adoption thresholds. Recommendation snapshot Resource and replica advice with sources, constraints, version, and expiry. Four operating modes Observe: collect, forecast, and compare without applying resource changes. Recommend: review resource and replica advice and its reasoning. Admission: apply authorized resource advice to new Pods. Auto: let the Operator adjust replicas within bounds, steps, and cooldowns. Usage boundaries The platform manages a single cluster, not cross-cluster migration. Read historical observations, capacity estimates, future forecasts, and actual Ready capacity separately. Estimated per-Pod capacity is not a measured maximum. Keep one replica controller per workload. Admission affects new Pods; running resource configurations require creation or rolling updates. Configure models and actions separately Prediction mode determines how advice is calculated: no prediction, a fixed algorithm, or dynamic algorithms. Operating mode determines permitted actions: Observe, Recommend, Admission, or Auto. Configure them independently to compare models while keeping cluster resources unchanged. New modules start with prediction disabled. Once enabled, fixed mode runs the selected method; dynamic mode uses enabled methods and combines their votes for dynamic replica decisions. See models and prediction modes for eligibility rules.

title: Metrics and data quality
summary: Connect sources, templates, and datasets to prepare dependable inputs.
text: Connect a Metrics source Add the source address, authentication, and connection settings. Check availability before defining metric templates. For Prometheus-compatible queries, confirm the selected series belong to the intended workload. Define metric templates Templates hold queries, variables, units, and aggregation. Modules reference them and render queries for their targets. Start with a built-in preset and adapt it to real cluster labels. Align CPU, memory, and request scope; distinguish workload totals from per-Pod use. Requests and limits are configuration; actual use is an observation. OOM, JVM heap pressure, and throttling provide additional protection signals. For empty queries, inspect labels, filters, the source, and time range. Datasets and historical quality Datasets align sample intervals, aggregation, conversion, precision, and gap handling. Inspect coverage, gaps, and freshness against model sample and season requirements. A gap is not zero demand Handle missing, invalid, and stale samples through explicit rules. Do not interpret gaps as falling demand. Recommendations should explain input quality and degradation. Units and time Specify conversions between cores and millicores, bytes and MiB, and counts and rates. Storage uses UTC; pages display UTC+8. Schedules use their explicitly configured IANA timezone.

title: Models and prediction modes
summary: Choose fixed or dynamic methods, explore models, corrections, and eligibility.
text: Forecasting methods The platform provides 15 built-in algorithms plus external model service integration, covering baselines, trends, seasonality, historical similarity, and combinations. Compare methods on the same workload windows using backtests and arriving actuals. Model What it captures Naive / Seasonal Naive Last-value continuation or repeated cycles as baselines. EWMA Short-term smoothing with emphasis on recent observations. Holt-Winters Level, trend, and seasonality with configurable damping and seasonal mode. Theta Smoothed level and trend for noisy sequences. MSTL Daily and weekly seasonal shapes. Seasonal Profile Time-of-day and weekday profiles using historical percentiles. Peak Envelope Changes in peak demand and resource high-water marks. Histogram Percentile Decayed historical percentiles for resource-sizing advice. KNN Similar past windows and their following trajectories. Ridge AR Lags, calendar features, and available covariates. Random Forest / GBDT Relationships between historical features and demand through regression trees. Combination Multiple member predictions combined with configured weighting and error handling. Method-by-method parameters and configuration Each method has its own parameter guide with defaults, types, ranges, units, history requirements, examples, and tuning tradeoffs. Configure external services in Model management and built-in methods in Algorithm management. Algorithm / model Guide Naive Repeats the latest observation across the horizon. Use it as a basic comparison and to check the data workflow; it cannot anticipate cycles or sudden changes. Seasonal Naive Repeats the corresponding observations from the preceding cycle. A seasonal baseline for repeating demand; anomalies in that cycle are repeated too. EWMA Smooths recent observations and projects the resulting level. A low-cost candidate for recent demand, without explicit daily seasonality. Damped Trend Estimates where a slow climb that has begun is heading from the newest stretch of history, with a slope that fades so the forecast converges to a ceiling. Suits memory and caches that creep up with sudden drops. Histogram Percentile Uses a time-decayed historical percentile as a constant future level. Useful for comparing high-water resource sizing, without predicting when a peak occurs. Random Forest Fits and averages regression trees on sampled historical features, supporting nonlinear relationships and covariates. More costly than simple statistical methods. KNN Finds similar historical windows and follows their subsequent trajectories. Useful for recurring shapes, with limited ability to anticipate patterns absent from history. Holt-Winters Models level, trend, and seasonality with additive or multiplicative seasons and optional damped trend. Suitable for cyclic demand with changing levels. Model service · forecasting and tuning Calls an external time-series model over HTTP. Configure it in Model management, then choose the module prediction mode. A failed request fails that candidate while other eligible methods continue. Theta Combines a smoothed level with half the fitted linear slope, optionally removing seasonality first. A candidate for noisy trends; forecasts are clamped at zero. MSTL Separates daily and weekly seasonal shapes and applies Theta to the remainder. This implementation iterates fixed seasonal shapes rather than time-varying LOESS components. Seasonal Profile Groups observations by time of day and optionally weekday, then uses a decayed percentile per bucket. Useful for weekday/weekend demand patterns. Peak Envelope Builds a rolling-maximum envelope and extrapolates its robust slope. Targets high-water demand rather than averages, such as memory sawtooth patterns and cache growth. Combination Combines member forecasts using a stepwise median or recent-error weights. The combination must earn backtest promotion like other candidates. Ridge AR Fits linear relationships from lags, optional UTC calendar features, and covariates. A relatively inexpensive machine-learning candidate for stable linear dependencies. GBDT Fits successive trees to residuals using lags, calendars, and covariates. Supports squared-error point forecasts or a native quantile objective. Before configuring a method Steps are not minutes: cycle steps = cycle seconds / sample interval seconds. At five-minute sampling, a day is 288 steps and a week 2016; forecast steps use the same interval. Defaults apply to new configuration, not to previously saved settings. Required fields have no default; omitted optional fields use defaults. Unknown names and invalid types are rejected. Separate method parameters from runtime policy. Configure history, sampling, and horizon on modules; configure model parameters, budgets, and eligibility centrally. JSON examples are parameter objects, not top-level config.yaml entries. Minimum history permits execution rather than guaranteeing accuracy. Direct forecasts, excluded KNN neighbors, and quantile calibration add history or compute requirements. Expand real history instead of duplicating observations. Quantile settings differ: percentile=95 is a historical percentile; quantile_level=0.9 enables conformal calibration. GBDT alpha and model-service service_quantile have their own meanings. Covariates do not provide future observations: only values before the forecast origin are used, and future steps carry the latest observation. Calendar features and KNN time filters use UTC; seasonal profiles use utc_offset_minutes. External models and background tuning Model services support finetune, unitshub_chronos, and unitshub_timesfm protocols. Configure a reachable endpoint first; only finetune supports background tuning. Forecasts do not wait for tuning: they use an existing tuned copy, or the pretrained model if none exists. Backtests and change replay assess pretrained models; use live prediction actuals to assess tuned copies. Full model service reference → Central model settings Manage activation, parameters, weights, budgets, and adoption thresholds centrally. Modules with prediction enabled in dynamic mode use the platform's enabled methods without separate instances or manual binding. Inspect model runs for insufficient history, missing parameters, and timeout. A rank or model name alone does not determine suitability. Central runtime settings Setting Meaning and use Activation Dynamic prediction uses enabled methods. Fixed mode still runs its selected method, so central activation does not replace the module prediction switch. Weight Affects scoring and ranking; default 1. It does not directly multiply predicted demand or guarantee adoption. Training time budget Zero uses the platform default. Positive values limit execution in seconds, up to 3600. Check this budget before adding trees, direct anchors, or calibration windows. A timed-out candidate fails. Promotion thresholds Minimum evaluated points, relative error improvement, and peak tolerance constrain candidates. Baselines need no promotion; quantile forecasts also use coverage and pinball loss. These settings belong to the model record, not the JSON parameter object. Central parameter changes affect multiple dynamic modules; compare backtests or change previews before saving. Derived and formula models Create derived models from built-in methods or define parameterized formulas. Check outputs and input requirements before saving. Parameter or implementation changes affect version identity and adoption eligibility. Choosing and adopting models Align forecast horizon and historical window, then compare resource error, peak underestimation, stability, and runtime. Available model forecasts can participate in look-ahead consensus; rank is not the sole basis for execution. Choose how a module predicts Prediction is disabled for new modules. History collection continues, recommendations use configured fallback defaults, and no algorithms run. Enable prediction when ready to use models, then choose a mode. Prediction mode How advice is produced When to use it No prediction Use fixed defaults without running algorithms; this is intentional configuration, not degradation. Collect history first or operate with known defaults. Fixed algorithm Run one selected algorithm without score-based switching. Non-baseline models still require backtest promotion. Keep a selected forecasting method explicit. Dynamic algorithms Run centrally enabled methods and use scores, recent errors, and eligibility. Dynamic replica decisions combine eligible candidates' votes. Compare methods continuously as workload patterns change. A fixed algorithm continues running for its module even when disabled centrally. It bypasses the module's minimum overall score filter, while version promotion and resource safeguards still apply. Prediction mode is independent of Observe, Recommend, Admission, and Auto: enabling a model does not authorize cluster writes. Keep seasonal models responsive For applicable seasonal and long-memory methods, recent predictions are compared with actuals. Significant rises add a short-term correction that fades over time. Downward correction is disabled by default to limit the risk of reacting to a brief dip. Combination forecasting also penalizes underestimation more heavily, trims much weaker members, and includes recent errors in its weights. Changes to models or correction parameters require renewed backtest promotion. Seasonal patterns and short-term corrections still operate within resource bounds and execution safeguards.

title: Naive
summary: Repeats the latest observation across the horizon. Use it as a basic comparison and to check the data workflow; it cannot anticipate cycles or sudden changes.
text: ← Models and prediction modes Purpose and workload fit Repeats the latest observation across the horizon. Use it as a basic comparison and to check the data workflow; it cannot anticipate cycles or sudden changes. History and runtime requirements At least one valid observation. Inputs must be regularly sampled, gap-free, and finite. Outputs retain the metric unit, such as CPU cores, memory bytes, or requests per second. The sample interval determines the duration of a step. Minimum history permits execution; it does not establish forecast quality. This method does not use covariates; target metrics are forecast separately. How it works and the formula The naive forecast (also called the random-walk forecast) does one thing: it takes the last observed value as the forecast for every future step. Formula Copy ŷ(T+h) = y(T) h = 1, 2, …, H y(T) is the newest value of the history, H the number of steps to forecast and h the step ahead. There are no parameters and nothing is trained. Why it is done this way: over minutes to tens of minutes a resource load is usually sticky: the likeliest next value is the current one, so this simplest forecast is often hard to beat over a short range. The platform uses it as the baseline: any more complex algorithm has to beat it in the backtest before it may be adopted. It also checks the collection and forecast chain (its curve should hug the actual values, one step late). What it cannot do: it sees no cycle and no coming rise or fall. When the load changes, it follows one forecast cycle late. Parameter reference No method-specific parameters; the parameter object is {} . Configuration example Edit parameters in Algorithm management. This is a parameter object, not a complete config.yaml. Seasonal examples assume five-minute sampling; adjust for your actual interval. Omitted optional values use the defaults above. JSON Copy {} Worked example: data, parameters and substitution Suppose the last 4 samples (one every 5 minutes) of the CPU usage of a service are as follows, in cores. We forecast the next 3 steps (15 minutes). Data Copy y = [0.8, 1.0, 1.2, 1.1] (the newest is the last one, 1.1) Substituting into the formula: Calculation Copy ŷ(T+1) = y(T) = 1.1 ŷ(T+2) = y(T) = 1.1 ŷ(T+3) = y(T) = 1.1 The result is [1.1, 1.1, 1.1] : a horizontal line at the last observed value. The earlier 0.8, 1.0 and 1.2 play no part. These numbers are computed by the real code in pkg/forecast/docs_examples_test.go and checked on every test run: if the algorithm changes and no longer matches this page, the test fails. Tuning and tradeoffs There are no algorithm parameters. Compare EWMA, Theta, or Seasonal Naive when trend or seasonality matters. Sources and references Hyndman, R.J. & Athanasopoulos, G. Forecasting: Principles and Practice (3rd ed., OTexts, 2021), section 5.2 "Some simple forecasting methods", the Naïve method: https://otexts.com/fpp3/simple-methods.html . Using it as the baseline of every candidate is the general practice in forecast evaluation: a new method means something only when it beats the naïve forecast (same book, section 5.8 on evaluating forecast accuracy). Use in a module Save parameters and check history, sample interval, and horizon. Enable module prediction. Fixed mode runs the selected method; dynamic mode uses centrally enabled methods. This baseline does not need backtest promotion, but actual performance still needs review. Review error, peak underestimation, runtime, and adoption reasons in Observe or Recommend before separately authorizing admission and replica actions. For insufficient history, invalid settings, timeouts, or invalid output, inspect run reasons. Without eligible forecasts, the module follows its schedules, fallback, and protection rules. Backtesting and evaluation · Recommendations and look-ahead

title: Seasonal Naive
summary: Repeats the corresponding observations from the preceding cycle. A seasonal baseline for repeating demand; anomalies in that cycle are repeated too.
text: ← Models and prediction modes Purpose and workload fit Repeats the corresponding observations from the preceding cycle. A seasonal baseline for repeating demand; anomalies in that cycle are repeated too. History and runtime requirements At least season_length_steps observations: one full cycle. Inputs must be regularly sampled, gap-free, and finite. Outputs retain the metric unit, such as CPU cores, memory bytes, or requests per second. The sample interval determines the duration of a step. Minimum history permits execution; it does not establish forecast quality. This method does not use covariates; target metrics are forecast separately. How it works and the formula The seasonal naive forecast takes the value at the same position one cycle earlier as the forecast. The cycle length m is in steps, given by season_length_steps ; the algorithm never guesses the cycle. Formula Copy ŷ(T+h) = y(T + h − m·(k+1)), where k = ⌊(h−1)/m⌋ In plain words: forecast step 1 is step 1 of the latest cycle, step 2 is step 2, and so on. When the forecast range is longer than a cycle, the latest cycle is repeated as a whole. In the code this is out[h] = values[n − m + (h mod m)] ( h from 0). You convert season_length_steps yourself: the length of the cycle ÷ the sampling step. A daily cycle at 5-minute samples = 24×60÷5 = 288 steps; a weekly cycle = 7×288 = 2016 steps. The history needs at least m points. Why it is done this way: many business loads have a strong daily or weekly cycle (a morning peak, a Monday batch). For such a load "what was it at this time yesterday" is often more accurate than "what is it now", and it takes almost no computation. It is the baseline of the seasonal algorithms. Its weakness: it looks at one cycle only. If that cycle happened to hold an incident or an odd peak, it copies the oddity into the future as if it were normal; it sees no trend either. That is why the platform lets it decide only when the history holds several full cycles (system parameter forecast.min_seasons , default 3), and why it should be compared with other algorithms. Parameter reference On narrow screens, swipe the parameter table horizontally to read all columns. Parameter / type Default / range / unit Meaning and use season_length_steps int Required; no default ≥ 2; steps Season length in sample steps; zero disables seasonality where allowed. Seasonal Naive requires an explicit cycle. Configuration example Edit parameters in Algorithm management. This is a parameter object, not a complete config.yaml. Seasonal examples assume five-minute sampling; adjust for your actual interval. Omitted optional values use the defaults above. JSON Copy { "season_length_steps": 288 } Worked example: data, parameters and substitution To keep it readable we use a "mini cycle" of 4 steps (in real use it is 288 or 2016). Samples are every 5 minutes and the history holds two full cycles: JSON Copy { "season_length_steps": 4 } Data Copy y = [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 2.0, 1.2, 2.2, 3.2, 2.1] └─ 1st cycle ─┘ └─ 2nd cycle (latest) ─┘ n = 8, m = 4 We forecast the next 6 steps. Take the latest cycle [1.2, 2.2, 3.2, 2.1] and apply values[n − m + (h mod m)] : h (from 0) h mod 4 index n−m+(h mod m) value taken 0 0 8−4+0 = 4 1.2 1 1 5 2.2 2 2 6 3.2 3 3 7 2.1 4 0 4 1.2 5 1 5 2.2 The result is [1.2, 2.2, 3.2, 2.1, 1.2, 2.2] : the latest cycle copied as it is. The values of the first cycle (1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 2.0) play no part, which is what "looks at one cycle only" means. These numbers are computed by the real code in pkg/forecast/docs_examples_test.go and checked on every test run. Tuning and tradeoffs Convert the business cycle into sample steps. A day is 288 steps at five-minute sampling or 1440 at one-minute sampling; 24 is not automatically a day. Sources and references Hyndman, R.J. & Athanasopoulos, G. Forecasting: Principles and Practice (3rd ed., OTexts, 2021), section 5.2, the Seasonal naïve method: https://otexts.com/fpp3/simple-methods.html . The platform rule that a seasonal algorithm may decide only with several cycles of history exists so that one odd cycle is not taken for a pattern; see the system parameter forecast.min_seasons . Use in a module Save parameters and check history, sample interval, and horizon. Enable module prediction. Fixed mode runs the selected method; dynamic mode uses centrally enabled methods. This baseline does not need backtest promotion, but actual performance still needs review. Review error, peak underestimation, runtime, and adoption reasons in Observe or Recommend before separately authorizing admission and replica actions. For insufficient history, invalid settings, timeouts, or invalid output, inspect run reasons. Without eligible forecasts, the module follows its schedules, fallback, and protection rules. Backtesting and evaluation · Recommendations and look-ahead

title: EWMA
summary: Smooths recent observations and projects the resulting level. A low-cost candidate for recent demand, without explicit daily seasonality.
text: ← Models and prediction modes Purpose and workload fit Smooths recent observations and projects the resulting level. A low-cost candidate for recent demand, without explicit daily seasonality. History and runtime requirements At least two observations. Inputs must be regularly sampled, gap-free, and finite. Outputs retain the metric unit, such as CPU cores, memory bytes, or requests per second. The sample interval determines the duration of a step. Minimum history permits execution; it does not establish forecast quality. This method does not use covariates; target metrics are forecast separately. How it works and the formula EWMA (exponentially weighted moving average, also called simple exponential smoothing) gives every historical value a weight: the newer the value the larger the weight, decaying by a fixed ratio. The forecast is the smoothed "current level", carried into the future. Formula Copy level recursion: ℓ(1) = y(1) ℓ(t) = α·y(t) + (1 − α)·ℓ(t−1) t = 2 … T forecast: ŷ(T+h) = ℓ(T) h = 1 … H (a flat line) equivalently: ℓ(T) = α·Σ (1−α)^k · y(T−k): the newest value weighs α, each step back multiplies by (1−α) How the parameters enter the formula: alpha (α, 0 to 1): the larger, the more the newest value counts. The effective "memory" is about 1/α steps: α=0.3 is roughly the last 3 steps and a bit more. span : another way to write it, α = 2 / (span + 1) . span=5 equals α=1/3. Give one of the two, not both. bias_correction : weight the history directly by (1−α)^age and divide by the sum of the weights, instead of starting the recursion at the first value. On a short history the first value does not pull the result. Why it is done this way: a measured load is noisy: taking the last value lets one spike mislead you, taking the mean of the whole history reacts too slowly. EWMA trades "keeping up" against "resisting noise" with one parameter, costs a single loop, and so is a cheap candidate, especially where the recent load matters most. What it cannot do: the forecast is a flat line, it neither extrapolates a trend nor knows a cycle. On a steadily rising load it is always a little low (it lags the trend). Parameter reference On narrow screens, swipe the parameter table horizontally to read all columns. Parameter / type Default / range / unit Meaning and use alpha float 0.3 ≥ 0.001; ≤ 1 Smoothing coefficient; larger values react faster. Use either explicit alpha or a positive span. span int 0 ≥ 0; ≤ 100000; steps Alternative EWMA span; a positive value derives alpha=2/(span+1). Do not also set alpha explicitly. bias_correction bool false No additional range Correct the EWMA initialization bias. Configuration example Edit parameters in Algorithm management. This is a parameter object, not a complete config.yaml. Seasonal examples assume five-minute sampling; adjust for your actual interval. Omitted optional values use the defaults above. JSON Copy { "alpha": 0.3, "bias_correction": false } Worked example: data, parameters and substitution The last 6 samples (one every 5 minutes) of a CPU usage in cores. Parameters: JSON Copy { "alpha": 0.3, "bias_correction": false } Data Copy y = [10, 12, 11, 15, 14, 16] Recursing from the first value with ℓ(t) = 0.3·y(t) + 0.7·ℓ(t−1) : t y(t) substitution ℓ(t) 1 10 ℓ(1) = y(1) 10.0000 2 12 0.3×12 + 0.7×10.0000 10.6000 3 11 0.3×11 + 0.7×10.6000 10.7200 4 15 0.3×15 + 0.7×10.7200 12.0040 5 14 0.3×14 + 0.7×12.0040 12.6028 6 16 0.3×16 + 0.7×12.6028 13.6220 So the forecast is [13.622, 13.622] (2 steps): a flat line. Note the last actual value is 16 while the forecast is 13.6: the smaller earlier values still pull it down. That is the price of smoothing, and why it comes out low on a rising load. See how the result changes with other parameters (same data): bias_correction: true : weigh directly with 1, 0.7, 0.49, 0.343, 0.2401, 0.16807 (the newest value weighs most) and average: 14.1049 . It is no longer tied to the first value 10, so it is higher. span: 5 (α = 2/6 ≈ 0.3333): 13.8601 , a little closer to the newest value than α=0.3. These numbers are computed by the real code in pkg/forecast/docs_examples_test.go and checked on every test run. Tuning and tradeoffs A larger alpha reacts faster but follows more noise. span is an alternative way to specify smoothing; do not supply explicit alpha together with a positive span. Sources and references Brown, R.G. Statistical Forecasting for Inventory Control (McGraw-Hill, 1959): the classic source of exponential smoothing. Hyndman, R.J. & Athanasopoulos, G. Forecasting: Principles and Practice (3rd ed., OTexts, 2021), section 8.1 Simple exponential smoothing: https://otexts.com/fpp3/ses.html . Hyndman, R.J. et al. Forecasting with Exponential Smoothing: The State Space Approach (Springer, 2008): the unifying theory of exponential smoothing. The conversion α = 2/(span+1) follows the convention of pandas ewm(span=…) .
